(1) The live Austin layer publishes an interim family with a leading 'I-' qualifier -- 14 values, 1,229 polygons -- which the predecessor's parser left unrecognised, costing 23,499 parcels (Hays 361, Williamson 6,108, Travis 17,030 at feature grain) that the previous reading had served under the base code; Austin's ordinance C2O-2009-017 and the city's 2016 development-standards table (20160616-041) give I-SF-2 the SF-2 standards, and the shipped austin-tx.json SF-2 row carries the same setback triple. Ruling: an interim district reads as its base through a declared leading-qualifier rule, with the interim fact disclosed on the stamped row. (2) The stamp CLI's `parcels read`/`parcels matched` count FEATURES (DISTINCT ON feature_index), not accounts, and in Travis 423,540 of 828,773 features carry prop_id '0'. Ruling: features with no CAD account are skipped and counted, and both the feature count and the account count are reported on every leg. The mission measured both rulings on the three Austin legs against LDT STAGING under a heavy-scan lease, without applying anything.

scopeBasis: The dispatch fixes the scope: legacy-design-tools, a fresh clone under P:/tmp registered to the property seat, the mission's branch, origin/main merged before a line was changed, work confined to the zoning acquisition path, the stamp run as a dry run only, no setback table edit, no store write, no serve change, no sub-agents. Deliberate exclusions a successor should not read as oversights: (1) NO SERVE CHANGE -- the ruling asks for the disclosure to be recorded, and the column plus provenance is the record; building a route would exceed the mission; (2) THE COUNTERS THEMSELVES ARE NOT RE-DENOMINATED -- accounts are printed beside features, but renaming or changing `parcels read` is the stamp owners' machinery and this lane does not own it; (3) THE 11TH FILE (the schema fixture template) is not scope creep but a prerequisite for the PR's own Test job, and it is justified in theHarnessTrap; (4) the census was READ, never re-derived, because P-255's instrument and grain are its own contract; (5) no migration was applied and no store written, even where the dry run could have applied it, because the integration seat owns that act.

fleetMemoryScratch.text: lib/db's integration harness (@workspace/db/testing -> withTestSchema) replays a hand-refreshed pg_dump fixture (lib/db/src/__tests__/__fixtures__/schema.sql.template) into its disposable schema; it does NOT read the drizzle schema. Adding a column to any drizzle table silently breaks every write-path integration test (SQLSTATE 42703) until the template gains the line, and CI fails the PR twice over (the drift check compares a pushed live database against the committed template). Refresh it in the same change.

Exporting DATABASE_URL arms every integration test in the repo, invisibly: they SKIP when it is unset and RUN when it is set, and withTestSchema then CREATEs and DROPs schemas in whatever store it names. A dry run and a test run in the same shell session means the suite inherits your deployment DSN. Use TEST_DATABASE_URL (the harness prefers it) or a throwaway container.

node on this Windows box cannot verify Google Frontend's TLS chain with its bundled CA store: fetch fails `unable to verify the first certificate`, and heavy-scan-lease.mjs reports it as `{"code":"FAILED","message":"fetch failed"}`, which reads like a credentials problem and is not one. Run node with --use-system-ca for the lease script and for any ArcGIS fetch.

The heavy-scan lease API is in project hauska-prod-497015 (Cloud Run service factory-control, us-east4, https://factory-control-h7gvu7rgcq-uk.a.run.app) with its key in Secret Manager FACTORY_CONTROL_API_KEY there -- NOT in legacy-design-tools-prod (which holds only FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO). The API looks leases up BY TOKEN; persist id + holderToken + expiry the moment you take one or release answers LEASE_LOST.
